window: Covering reporting published since the Sept 18 edition, roughly Sept 17-19, with a couple of incident dates running back to Sept 14-15 where reporting lagged. No new SOUTHCOM/JTF-WHEM lethal strike or refueling-vessel interdiction was found in this window, so the standing cumulative tally stays at 69 strikes and at least 230 deaths, and the second Los Choneros refueling-vessel interdiction already logged Sept 18 remains the most recent military action. A widely-surfacing 'Marinha e PF fazem maior apreensao de cocaina no mar brasileiro' story about a 3.6-tonne Pernambuco cocaine bust and the vessel 'Palmares 1' looked like fresh Sept 19 news in search results but checked out, on the publishing outlet's own byline, as a September 2023 case being re-surfaced — it was dropped. Two other apparent Sept 17-18 stories collapsed the same way on verification: an Argentina Gendarmeria Brazo Largo cocaine seizure recirculating with a Sept 18 dateline was actually from Sept 3, and a Colombian de la Espriella daily security tally recirculating with a Sept 18 dateline was actually from Sept 2; both were dropped as stale. A Spanish Costa del Sol cocaine case with the same headline numbers as the Sept 17 Albanian-network story that is included below appears to be the same investigation surfacing under an inconsistent April dateline on one aggregator; it was published independently on Sept 17 by three Colombian outlets, so it is included, sourced to the more consistent reporting. A Katie Williams/Kenneth Smith DC fentanyl case that a search summary initially dated to Sept 18 turned out, on the original blog's own reporting, to be a Aug 18 arrest and was dropped as stale.
